nominations.basis: Probed 2026-09-18 with scripts/probe_candidate_pages.py: 7,835 readable characters and the verifier's own label test matched in the content region as "Office for Civil Rights (OCR) | U.S. Department of Education", which is the curated name exactly. This is OCR's own page under the department's domain.

Probed 2026-09-18: 3,664 readable characters; the label test matched in the content region as "Office for Civil Rights (OCR)". This is the department's own enumeration of its offices ("Each of ED's 17 offices"), so a confirmation from it evidences the exec-dept-ed -> exec-dept-ed-ocr edge as well as the unit. The prior pass declined this node covered_by_parent on the belief that www.ed.gov refuses this crawler; it does not - it was read four times today.

note: ED's own complete office list was read and carries no regional layer at all. The page's own wording is "Each of ED's 17 offices play a vital role" and "ED's Operating Structure", and it then names all seventeen - FSA, IES, OCIO, OCO, OCR, OCTAE, ODS, OELA, OESE, OFO, OGC, OLCA, OPE, OPEPD, OS, OSERS, OUS (page last reviewed August 18, 2026). No numbered region, and no word 'Region', appears. I also read https://www.ed.gov/ (2,808 chars), https://www.ed.gov/about (2,101), https://www.ed.gov/about/ed-offices/oco (12,729 chars - OCO is the office that historically ran ED's regional outreach, and the string 'egion' occurs zero times in it) and https://www.ed.gov/about/ed-offices/ofo (27,825 chars). www2.ed.gov, which used to host /about/contacts/gen/regions.html, answers 403. This is a curated-structure problem, not a URL problem: the curated name 'Dept of Education Region I - New England' is a graph construction and the department publishes no such unit today.

note: 'Other Independent Agencies (25+)' is this graph's catch-all bucket, not a body the government names. The project's own matcher agrees without a fetch: uncheckable_reason_for_node returns 'curated_count_label' for it, so verify_base_graph.py would never check it even if a page were queued.

The Smithsonian publishes at si.edu, which the verifier refuses by host rule - this is the runbook's own worked example for this reason. It already carries a Federal Register directory listing (https://www.federalregister.gov/agencies/smithsonian-institution), which is a different kind of evidence and the only .gov route to it.

The Postal Service's own site is usps.com (and about.usps.com); neither is a .gov or .mil host, so the verifier will not fetch either. uspsoig.gov exists but is the Inspector General, a different unit from the corporation itself. The node's Federal Register directory listing (https://www.federalregister.gov/agencies/postal-service) is the only .gov evidence available for it.

The judiciary does not use this heading. uscourts.gov's own structure page was read (3,184 readable chars) and groups these bodies under the heading "Article I Courts", whose own sentence is "Congress created several Article I that are not part of the Third Branch. Article I Courts include:" followed by the U.S. Court of Appeals for Veterans Claims, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Armed Forces and the U.S. Tax Court. 'Specialized Federal Courts' appears nowhere on that page, on uscourts.gov's home page (1,988 chars) or on /about-federal-courts (443 chars). A curator wanting this grouping to be nameable would rename it 'Article I Courts', but the six children are each real courts with their own sites and that is where the evidence is.

A curated umbrella over the Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts, the Federal Judicial Center, the Sentencing Commission and the Federal Public Defender offices. The judiciary names each of those individually and has no collective name for them: uscourts.gov's home page (1,988 readable chars), /about-federal-courts (443) and /about-federal-courts/court-role-and-structure (3,184) were all read today and none carries 'Judicial Support Organizations' as a heading, link or list item.

This node is a per-VISN template - one node standing for every medical center inside VISN 16 - rather than a named facility, so no page can label it, and four VA pages read today confirm the government uses different words. VA's own department page says "VA's Veterans Health Administration is the largest integrated health care network in the United States, with 1,255 health care facilities serving 9 million enrolled Veterans each year"; it names the Veterans Health Administration, not any unit called 'VA Medical Centers'. Also read: https://www.va.gov/health/ (9,441 chars), https://www.va.gov/health/visns.asp (1,722) and https://www.va.gov/directory/guide/home.asp (1,766), none of which labels the curated name. VISN 16's own site, https://www.visn16.va.gov/, cannot be used either: its robots.txt could not be reached at all (URLError), which this project treats as a complete disallow. The fix is curation - name the individual medical centers, or drop the template - not another URL.

probe.detail: 7,430 readable characters, well above the floor; the verifier's label test found no fragment equal to 'VA Medical Centers' in content or navigation. The page's own wording for this part of VA is "Veterans Health Administration" with "1,255 health care facilities".

note: CIA's own organization page was read in full and lists exactly five directorates under the heading "Directorates": "Directorate of Analysis", "Directorate of Operations", "Directorate of Science and Technology", "Directorate of Mission Systems", "Directorate of Support". Four of those match curated sibling nodes; the fifth, "Directorate of Mission Systems", has no node in this graph, and 'Directorate of Digital Innovation' has no place on the page. The page's own framing is "Our Agency is made up of five broad disciplines, known as Directorates". So the graph's DDI node and CIA's Directorate of Mission Systems are almost certainly the same unit under its current name - but that is a rename to argue in CURATION.md from this page's wording, not something a different URL can fix. cia.gov/about/organization/directorate-of-digital-innovation/ returns 404.

note: The committee's own site was read and its Subcommittees menu enumerates seven: "Cybersecurity, Information Technology, and Government Innovation", "Economic Growth, Energy Policy, and Regulatory Affairs", "Government Operations", "Health Care and Financial Services", "Military and Foreign Affairs", "Federal Law Enforcement", "Delivering on Government Efficiency" (plus two named Task Forces). None is this one; 'National Security, the Border & Foreign Affairs' was a 118th-Congress subcommittee and the committee no longer carries it. The likely successor for the foreign-affairs half is the page's "Military and Foreign Affairs", which the graph already has as a separate node, so this looks like a stale node to retire rather than rename. Two further facts for the curator from the same read: the deep link https://oversight.house.gov/subcommittee/national-security-the-border-and-foreign-affairs-subcommittee/ returns 404, and the page's own footer says "Committee on Oversight and Government Reform", not the graph's 'Oversight & Accountability'.
